mainTopic: Placing חטאת blood on the corners of the מזבח, the red line dividing the מזבח, and which side of the יסוד gets the leftover blood
overview: The משנה describes how the כהן goes around the four corners of the מזבח with the blood of an outer חטאת, pours the leftover blood on the southern יסוד, and says male כהנים eat the meat in the courtyard until midnight. The גמרא asks how exactly the blood is put on a corner. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree: one allows a cubit on either side, and the other requires the blood right at the corner's point. The גמרא says this argument only exists according to רבי. It answers a challenge from a ברייתא by explaining that the point is the ideal way, and a cubit to either side still works. It then quotes the ברייתא where רבי allows anywhere above the red line, while רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון requires an animal חטאת to go on the corner itself. רבי אבהו finds רבי's source in a פסוק in יחזקאל, which the גמרא reads as giving the corners a 'domain' of four אמות. Next comes the source for the red line: the רשת reaching halfway up the מזבח. Finally, the גמרא discusses which side of the יסוד gets the leftover blood, bringing a ברייתא and the views of רבי ישמעאל (west) and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי (south), with רבי אסי explaining the southern view.

steps.title: The route around the altar's four corners
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the כהן going up the ramp and putting the חטאת blood on the four corners in a fixed order.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went up the ramp, turned onto the ledge that runs around the altar, and came to the southeast corner, then the northeast, then the northwest, then the southwest.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out the order in which the כהן puts the blood of an outer חטאת on the four corners of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן goes up the ramp on the south side and turns right onto the סובב. He walks around the מזבח, starting at the southeast corner and ending at the southwest corner. Each corner gets its own placement of blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the altar
The ledge that runs all the way around the altar
A corner (literally 'horn') of the altar

phrases.english: He went up the ramp and turned to the surrounding ledge,
and came to the southeast corner,
then the northeast,
then the northwest, then the southwest.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חטאת blood is placed on all four corners, going around from southeast to northeast to northwest to southwest.

steps.title: Leftover blood and the eating of the meat
steps.stepSummary: The leftover blood is poured on the southern base, and the meat is eaten by male כהנים inside the courtyard until midnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would pour the leftover blood on the southern base. The meat is eaten inside the curtains, by male כהנים, cooked any way, for that day and the night after, until midnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the laws of the חטאת: what to do with the remaining blood, and the rules for eating the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the four corners, the remaining blood is poured on the יסוד on the south side. Only male כהנים may eat the meat, only inside the courtyard, prepared in any style. The time limit is the day it was brought and the following night, up to חצות.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood left over after the required placements
The base of the altar
The curtains around the courtyard; 'inside the curtains' means inside the courtyard
Male כהנים
Midnight

steps.whatToRemember: The outer חטאת gets blood on all four corners, and its leftover blood goes on the southern יסוד. Male כהנים eat it in the courtyard until midnight.

phrases.english: The leftover blood he would pour
on the southern base,
and they are eaten inside the curtains
by the males of the priesthood, in any kind of preparation,
for the day and the night, until midnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם הָיָה שׁוֹפֵךְ עַל יְסוֹד דְּרוֹמִית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leftover blood goes on the southern יסוד. The meat is eaten in the courtyard by male כהנים, in any preparation, until midnight.

steps.title: How exactly is the blood put on the corner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the כהן actually performs the placement on each corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a short question that sets up the argument coming next: how exactly is the blood placed on a corner?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the blood goes on each corner but did not say exactly where on the corner. The גמרא wants to know how precise the כהן has to be.

keyTerms.meaning: How does he do it?

phrases.english: Gemara: How does he do it?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact way and place the כהן puts the blood on each corner of the מזבח.

steps.title: A cubit on each side, or right at the point
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree: one allows a cubit on either side of the corner, and the other requires the blood to go right at the corner's point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree. One says he puts it within a cubit this way or a cubit that way. The other says he applies it and moves downward right opposite the point of the corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a disagreement between two אמוראים about how exact the placement must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view gives the כהן room: anywhere within one cubit on either side of the corner counts. The second view is strict: the blood must go right at the sharp edge of the corner, so that it runs down both sides. The גמרא does not say which אמורא holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit this way and a cubit that way
Applies the blood of the חטאת
The sharp point or edge of the corner

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא never tells us which of the two holds which view. It only says 'one says' and 'one says.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar disagree;

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: נוֹתֵן אַמָּה אֵילָךְ וְאַמָּה אֵילָךְ,
phrases.english: one says: he places it within a cubit this way or a cubit that way,
and one says: he applies the blood and moves downward
opposite the point of the corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר; חַד אָמַר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a disagreement. One view allows a cubit on either side of the corner; the other requires the blood right at the corner's point.

steps.title: The argument is only according to רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון there is no argument; the two אמוראים argue only according to רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says the placement itself is done only on the actual body of the corner, everyone agrees. Where they disagree is according to רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument and shows exactly which earlier view the two אמוראים are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון requires the blood to go on the corner block itself, so anywhere on it is fine, and there is nothing to argue about. רבי does not require the blood to be on the corner block itself. So according to him we must ask how far from the corner still counts as 'opposite the corner.'

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
The actual body of the corner
Everyone agrees
Where they do disagree

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
who says: it itself,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the placement of the חטאת blood.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ נַעֲשֵׂית אֶלָּא בְּגוּפָהּ שֶׁל קֶרֶן –
phrases.english: is done only on the actual body of the corner,
everyone agrees;
where they disagree is according to Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the argument from step 4 to the view of רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, there is no argument. The two אמוראים argue only according to רבי.

steps.title: What counts as 'opposite the corner'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reasoning: one holds a cubit on each side still counts as opposite the corner, and the other holds only the point itself counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that a cubit this way and a cubit that way still counts as opposite the corner. The other holds that opposite its point, yes; anything further, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the reasoning behind each of the two views, according to רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree, according to רבי, that the blood must be 'opposite the corner.' They argue only about how wide that area is. Is it a cubit in either direction, or only the exact edge?

keyTerms.meaning: One master holds
Yes
More than that, no

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, the argument is whether 'opposite the corner' includes a cubit on each side, or only the exact point.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: אַמָּה אֵילָךְ וְאַמָּה אֵילָךְ –
phrases.english: One master holds: a cubit this way and a cubit that way
still counts as opposite the corner;

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: כְּנֶגֶד חוּדָּהּ אִין, טְפֵי לָא.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: opposite its point, yes; more than that, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: אַמָּה אֵילָךְ וְאַמָּה אֵילָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of each side, now that step 5 placed the argument according to רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is about how wide 'opposite the corner' is: a cubit on each side, or only the exact point.

steps.title: A ברייתא describes the blood going right at the point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא describing the חטאת blood being applied right at the point of each corner. This seems to challenge the view that allows a cubit on each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: for a communal or individual חטאת, how is the blood placed? He would go up the ramp, turn onto the ledge, and come to the southeast corner. He dips his right index finger in the blood in the bowl, steadies it with his thumb above and his little finger below, and applies the blood moving down opposite the point of the corner, until all the blood on his finger is used up. He does the same at every corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge from a ברייתא that describes the placement as happening right at the point of the corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same wording as the strict view: 'מחטא ויורד כנגד חודה של קרן.' That seems to say the blood must go right at the point, and not anywhere within a cubit. So the lenient view appears to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: The placement of their blood
The most skilled finger of the right hand (the index finger)
The bowl that holds the blood
Steadies or gathers (the blood on the finger)

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is aimed only at the view that allows a cubit on each side. The strict view matches the ברייתא's wording exactly.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: communal and individual sin offerings,
how is their blood placed?
He would go up the ramp and turn to the surrounding ledge,
and come to the southeast corner;
and he dips his right finger, the most skilled finger of the right hand,
into the blood that is in the bowl;
and he steadies it with his thumb from above
and with his little finger from below,

phrases.aramaic: וּמְחַטֵּא וְיוֹרֵד כְּנֶגֶד חוּדָּהּ שֶׁל קֶרֶן,
phrases.english: and he applies the blood, moving downward, opposite the point of the corner,
until he uses up all the blood on his finger.
And the same at each and every corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lenient view explained in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the blood may go anywhere within a cubit on either side of the corner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the blood is applied 'opposite the point of the corner,' which suggests only the exact point is valid, not a cubit on each side.

steps.title: The point of the corner is only the ideal way
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that describes placing the blood on the point of the corner is talking about the best way to do the מצוה. Placing it a cubit to either side still works after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: the best way to do the מצוה is on the point of the corner. But if he put the blood a cubit to this side or a cubit to that side, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 7 by explaining that the ברייתא only describes the ideal way to do the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to require the point of the corner, which would go against the view that allows a cubit on each side. The answer splits the law into two levels: the point is the best way (לכתחילה), and a cubit to either side still counts (בדיעבד). So the ברייתא does not argue with the lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. The גמרא is about to reread a source.
Its sharp point or edge. Here, the tip of the corner.
We have no problem with it. It is still valid.

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say the point of the corner is unimportant. It is still the best way. It only says that a cubit to either side does not ruin the מצוה.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא from step 7 that described the blood going right at the point.

phrases.english: the ideal מצוה is on its point;

phrases.aramaic: אִי עֲבַד אַמָּה אֵילָךְ וְאַמָּה אֵילָךְ –
phrases.english: if he did it a cubit this way or a cubit that way,
we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge brought in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source as describing the ideal way (לכתחילה), not the minimum requirement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא requires the blood to be placed exactly at the point of the corner.
steps.terutzMaskana: The point is the best way, but a cubit to either side is still valid.

steps.title: What do רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact views of רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, which were mentioned in step 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the view of רבי, and what is the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks where the argument between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, mentioned earlier, actually comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the גמרא said the אמוראים argue only according to רבי, and not according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. To understand that, we need to know exactly what each תנא says. This question opens the search for that source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A question asking for content or a source.

phrases.english: What is the view of Rabbi,
and what is the view of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבִּי וּמַאי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the two תנאים named in step 5 and asks for their views.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and content of the argument between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי: upper bloods go anywhere above the red line
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי: blood meant for the upper part of the מזבח can go anywhere above the red line, and blood meant for the lower part can go anywhere below it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: blood meant for the top part of the מזבח is placed from the red line and up. Blood meant for the bottom part is placed from the red line and down. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. This first part gives רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gives a wide area: anywhere above the red line counts for the upper bloods. That is why, according to רבי, there is room for the אמוראים to argue about how far from the point of the corner the blood may go.

keyTerms.meaning: The red line painted around the middle of the מזבח. It divides the upper half from the lower half.
Bloods that must be placed on the upper half of the מזבח, like the blood of a חטאת.
Bloods that must be placed on the lower half of the מזבח.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
the upper bloods are placed
from the red line and above;
the lower bloods are placed
from the red line and below.
These are the words of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: דָּמִים הָעֶלְיוֹנִים נִיתָּנִין מִחוּט הַסִּיקְרָא וּלְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 with רבי's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי holds that upper bloods may be placed anywhere above the red line.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: an animal חטאת goes on the corner itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון limits רבי's rule to a bird עולה. An animal חטאת must be placed on the actual corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: when was this said? For a bird עולה. But an animal חטאת may only be placed on the body of the corner itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says the wide 'above the red line' rule is only for a bird עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an animal חטאת, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון requires the corner itself. That explains step 5: according to him, everyone agrees the blood goes right on the corner, so there is no argument. The אמוראים can argue only according to רבי, who allows a wider area.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? This phrase limits an earlier rule.
A bird brought as an עולה.
An animal brought as a חטאת.
The actual body of the corner.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: anywhere above the red line is fine. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: an animal חטאת must go on the corner itself. That is why the אמוראים argue only according to רבי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
In what case were these words said?
With a bird burnt offering;
but with an animal sin offering,
it itself is not done
except on the body of the corner itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by giving the second תנא's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון limits רבי's rule to a bird עולה and requires an animal חטאת to go on the corner itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why, in step 5, the argument of the אמוראים exists only according to רבי.

steps.title: רבי אבהו brings רבי's source from יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says רבי's source is the פסוק in יחזקאל describing the הראל, the top of the מזבח, as four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: What is רבי's reason? As it is written: 'And the הראל is four אמות, and from the הראל and up are the four corners.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a פסוק as the source for רבי's flexible view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק connects a measurement of four אמות to the corners at the top of the מזבח. רבי אבהו uses it to show that the area for placing the blood is wider than the corner's point. How exactly the פסוק shows this will be worked out in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?
A name for the top part of the מזבח in יחזקאל.
And so on. The rest of the פסוק continues.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
What is the reason of Rabbi?
As it is written:
"And the altar-top is four cubits,
and from the altar-top and above," etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says "are the four corners."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for רבי's view quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי's flexible view is based on the פסוק in יחזקאל linking four אמות to the corners.

steps.title: Was the מזבח only four אמות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the מזבח was much larger than four אמות, so what does the פסוק mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: Was it really only four אמות?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plain reading of the פסוק, because the מזבח was much bigger than four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק were simply giving the size of the מזבח, it would be wrong, since the מזבח was far larger. So the 'four אמות' must be measuring something else. This pushes the גמרא to find what the four אמות refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: Was it? Here it is said with surprise.

phrases.english: Was it only four cubits?!
phrases.notes: He means the מזבח itself was much bigger, so "four cubits" can't be its size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the plain meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of 'four אמות' in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מזבח was much larger than four אמות, so the פסוק cannot be giving its size.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: the corners' area is four
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה suggests that the four אמות is the area of the four corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: the place of the corners is four.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that the 'four אמות' measures the space taken up by the corners, not the whole מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each corner was about one square אמה, so he suggests the four corners together add up to four. This turns the measurement from the whole מזבח to just the corners.

keyTerms.meaning: The space the corners take up.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
And the place of the corners is four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: וּמְקוֹם קְרָנוֹת אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading what the measurement in the פסוק refers to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The four אמות is the size of the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The four אמות is the area of the four corners.

steps.title: The corners do not add up to four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the corners' area is not really four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was the place of the corners really four?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אדא בר אהבה's reading, because the corners together did not measure four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measurements of the corners do not actually reach four אמות, so 'the place of the corners' cannot be what the פסוק means. A different reading is needed.

phrases.english: Was the place of the corners four?!
phrases.notes: The corners put together are smaller than that, so this reading doesn't fit either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's reading that the corners' area is four.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The corners together do not actually measure four אמות.

steps.title: The corners' area of influence is four אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the פסוק: the domain belonging to the corners stretches four אמות, so blood placed within that area counts as on the corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: the domain of the corners is four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final reading of the פסוק: the four אמות is the area that 'belongs' to the corners, not their physical size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood placed within four אמות below the actual corner still counts as placed on the corner. This gives רבי his source for allowing blood anywhere above the red line, instead of only on the corner's body.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say. This brings in a corrected reading.
The domain or area that belongs to the corners.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, the corner's 'domain' stretches four אמות. So the blood of a חטאת does not have to be on the corner itself. Anywhere in that area above the red line counts.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
the domain of the corners is four.
phrases.notes: He means blood put within four cubits below the corner still counts as "on the corner."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading in step 14 after the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading 'four' as the corners' domain instead of their physical size.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The four אמות is the physical area of the corners.
steps.terutzMaskana: The four אמות is the area belonging to the corners, so blood placed there counts as on the corner.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the source for רבי's view that the upper bloods can go anywhere above the red line.

steps.title: A red line divided the altar in half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in מסכת מדות: a red line went around the middle of the מזבח to separate upper blood from lower blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: a red line wrapped around the middle of the מזבח, to separate the blood that goes on the top half from the blood that goes on the bottom half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה about a red line around the middle of the מזבח. This sets up the next question about where this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some קרבנות have their blood put on the upper half of the מזבח, and some on the lower half. The red line showed the כהן exactly where the halfway point was.

keyTerms.meaning: A red line (painted around the altar)
Blood that is placed on the upper half of the מזבח
Blood that is placed on the lower half of the מזבח

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" means in a different מסכת, here מסכת מדות.

phrases.english: A red line
wraps around it in the middle,
to separate between the upper bloods
and the lower bloods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the red line mentioned in רבי's ברייתא in step 10, and brings the משנה that describes it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A red line around the middle of the מזבח separates upper blood from lower blood.

steps.title: Where does the red line come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the dividing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the red-line rule. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know what in the Torah shows that the מזבח has a set upper half and lower half.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these words?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for dividing the מזבח into upper and lower halves.

steps.title: The net reaching halfway up is the divider
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב קטינא learns it from the פסוק that the רשת reaches halfway up the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב קטינא said: as it says, "and the net shall reach halfway up the מזבח." The Torah gave a divider to separate the upper blood from the lower blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר רב קטינא answers that the source is the פסוק about the רשת reaching halfway up the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah puts a net at the exact halfway point of the מזבח. That shows the Torah itself marked a border there, and the red line is what marks it.

keyTerms.meaning: The net or grating of the מזבח
Halfway up the מזבח
A divider or separation

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא,
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Ketina said,
as it is said: "And the net shall be
up to half of the altar" –
the Torah gave a divider
to separate between the upper bloods
and the lower bloods.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רשת reaching halfway up the מזבח is a Torah-given divider between upper and lower blood.

steps.title: Leftover blood goes on the southern base
steps.stepSummary: Returning to our משנה about שירי הדם, a ברייתא says the "base of the altar" means the southern יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה said: "the leftover blood, etc." The רבנן taught: "at the base of the altar" — this is the southern base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה, which says leftover blood is poured on the southern יסוד. It quotes a ברייתא that reads the פסוק this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says "base of the altar" without saying which side. The ברייתא states that it means the southern side, and will now test that claim.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood after the main placements
The base of the מזבח
The southern side of the base

phrases.english: The leftover blood, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which says the leftover blood is poured on the southern base.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "At the base of the altar" –
this is the southern base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section about a different line of our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leftover blood of the outer חטאת is poured on the southern יסוד.

steps.title: Maybe it means the western base instead?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: maybe it is the western יסוד, since we could learn the unclear פסוק from the clear one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it is the southern base? Or maybe it is only the western base, and we should learn the unclear פסוק from the clear one?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests its own claim by suggesting the western יסוד instead. It gives a reason: learn the unclear פסוק from a clear one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another פסוק, about blood brought inside, clearly says the leftover goes on the base that is by the entrance of the אהל מועד, which is the western side. So maybe the unclear "base" here also means the western side.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say...? (testing a claim)
The western side of the base
Unclear, not spelled out
Clear, spelled out

steps.confusionAlert: The line "let the unclear be learned from the clear" is part of the question here. It is the reason for saying western, not the ברייתא's final answer.

phrases.english: You say this is the southern base;
or is it only the western base,
and let the unclear be learned from the clear?
phrases.notes: The clear one is the פסוק about the inner blood, poured at the base by the entrance of the אהל מועד, which is the western side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר זֶה יְסוֹד דְּרוֹמִי; אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא יְסוֹד מַעֲרָבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the claim of step 20 by offering the western side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why say southern, when the clear פסוק about inner blood points to the western side?

steps.title: He pours on the side closest to him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers: compare the כהן coming down the ramp to the כהן coming out of the היכל. Both pour on the side nearest them, so here it is the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say: learn his coming down from the ramp from his coming out of the היכל. Just as when he comes out of the היכל he pours on the side closest to him, so too when he comes down the ramp he pours on the side closest to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the real lesson from the clear פסוק is "pour on the nearest side." For the outer מזבח, the nearest side is the south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coming out of the היכל, the first side of the מזבח the כהן reaches is the western one. Coming down the כבש, which is on the south, the first side he reaches is the southern one. So the same rule, "closest side," gives a different side in each case.

keyTerms.meaning: You can say (introducing the answer)
The ramp going up to the מזבח
The Sanctuary building
On the side closest to him

steps.whatToRemember: The rule for leftover blood is "pour on the nearest side of the יסוד": western for blood brought inside, southern for blood on the outer מזבח.

phrases.english: You can say: let his descent from the ramp be learned
from his exit from the Sanctuary;

phrases.aramaic: מָה יְצִיאָתוֹ מִן הַהֵיכָל – בְּסָמוּךְ לוֹ,
phrases.english: just as with his exit from the Sanctuary – on the side close to him,
phrases.notes: Walking out of the היכל, the side of the מזבח he reaches first is the western side.

phrases.aramaic: אַף יְרִידָתוֹ מִן הַכֶּבֶשׁ – בְּסָמוּךְ לוֹ.
phrases.english: so too with his descent from the ramp – on the side close to him.
phrases.notes: The ramp is on the south, so coming down it, the closest side is the south.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתָּ: יִלְמַד יְרִידָתוֹ מִן הַכֶּבֶשׁ לִיצִיאָתוֹ מִן הַהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 and keeps the claim of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: What we learn from the clear פסוק is "the nearest side," which for the outer מזבח means the southern יסוד.

steps.title: A dispute: all on the west, or all on the south
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל says both kinds of leftover blood go on the western יסוד; רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says both go on the southern יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי ישמעאל says: both this and that go on the western base. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: both this and that go on the southern base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא where two תנאים disagree with the first ברייתא's split. Each one puts all leftover blood on a single side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא split the cases: inner blood goes west, outer blood goes south. רבי ישמעאל puts both on the west, and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי puts both on the south.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that (both kinds of leftover blood)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows there are three views on where leftover blood goes: the first ברייתא splits the cases, רבי ישמעאל puts all of it on the west, and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי puts all of it on the south.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yishmael says:
this and that – the western base.
phrases.notes: "This and that" means the leftover blood from inside the היכל and the leftover blood from the outer מזבח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
this and that – the southern base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings two views that disagree with the split taught in steps 20-22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: all leftover blood goes on the western יסוד. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: all of it goes on the southern יסוד.

steps.title: The western view is clear, so what is the reason for the southern view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the western-base opinion makes sense, because it learns the unclear from the clear. It then asks for the reason behind the southern-base opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the one who says western base holds that we learn the unclear פסוק from the clear one. But the one who says southern base, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first agrees that רבי ישמעאל's western-base view is easy to understand. Then it asks what reason רבי שמעון בן יוחאי has for saying southern. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The western view is based on the rule יִלְמַד סָתוּם מִן הַמְּפוֹרָשׁ. The clear פסוק about blood from inside the היכל puts it at the base by the entrance of the אהל מועד, which seems to be the western יסוד, so the outer blood is read the same way. The southern view puts even the inner blood on the south, so the גמרא wants to know how he reads that clear פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted. This part makes sense, but the next part does not yet.
The western base of the מזבח
The southern base of the מזבח
Let the unclear be learned from the clear
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says the western base,
he holds: let the unclear be learned from the explicit.
But according to the one who says the southern base,
what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons behind the two opinions in the ברייתא of step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reason for the southern-base view.

steps.title: רבי אסי: this תנא holds the whole מזבח stands in the north
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי explains that the southern-base תנא pictures the entire מזבח as standing in the northern half of the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: This תנא holds that the whole מזבח stands in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers the question. The southern-base תנא pictures the whole מזבח in the northern half of the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole מזבח is in the north, then its southern side lines up with the middle of the courtyard, right in front of the entrance to the היכל. So the clear פסוק's words "פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד" (the entrance of the Tent), said about the blood from inside, themselves point to the southern יסוד. That is why this תנא says 'זה וזה', both kinds of leftover blood, go on the southern יסוד.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה-era sage. Here it means רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
The entire מזבח stands in the north

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the מזבח is outside the courtyard. It means the מזבח sits in the northern half, so its south edge is in the center, facing the היכל's door.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said,
This Tanna holds:
the entire altar stands in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי, קָסָבַר הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The southern-base תנא holds the whole מזבח is in the north, so the southern יסוד faces the היכל's entrance.

steps.title: Another version: the whole entrance stands in the south
steps.stepSummary: A second version of רבי אסי's answer says the entire entrance of the היכל stands toward the south, facing the southern part of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: the whole entrance stands in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way that רבי אסי's answer was reported. In this version the entrance of the היכל is the thing placed toward the south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions reach the same result: the southern יסוד is the part of the מזבח that faces the היכל's door. The first version describes it by where the מזבח sits. The second describes it by where the entrance sits. Either way, a כהן coming out of the היכל meets the southern side first.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same statement
The entrance, here the door of the היכל

steps.whatToRemember: The western view learns the unclear פסוק from the clear one. The southern view, according to רבי אסי, holds that the southern יסוד is the side facing the היכל's entrance, so it is the "פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד" of the פסוק.

phrases.english: Another version:
the entire entrance stands in the south.
phrases.notes: He means the היכל's door lines up with the southern part of the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second way of reporting רבי אסי's answer from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The היכל's entrance is placed toward the south, facing the southern יסוד.
